questions.q: Under the 'Doctrine of Waiver', can a citizen in India waive their Fundamental Rights?
questions.e: The doctrine of waiver is not applicable to fundamental rights in India; a citizen cannot waive their fundamental rights as they are mandatory obligations.

questions.q: Which doctrine deals with the "prospective" nature of the provision under Article 13(1) regarding pre-constitution laws?
questions.e: The doctrine of eclipse is based on the prospective nature of Article 13(1) regarding pre-constitution laws that are inconsistent with fundamental rights.

questions.q: The 'Doctrine of Pith and Substance' was evolved to determine the competence of the legislature when there is:
o: A conflict between fundamental rights and duties
An overlap between the Union and State lists
questions.e: The doctrine of pith and substance is applied when the legislative powers of the Centre and States overlap, to determine the true nature and character of a law.

questions.q: Which doctrine states that what cannot be done directly cannot be done indirectly?
questions.e: The doctrine of colourable legislation is based on the maxim "you cannot do indirectly, what you cannot do directly".

questions.q: According to the 'Doctrine of Precedent', a judgment of which court is binding on all other courts in India?
questions.e: Article 141 provides that the law declared by the Supreme Court shall be binding on all courts within the territory of India.

questions.q: The 'Doctrine of Occupied Field' is relevant in the case of laws made with reference to which list?
questions.e: The doctrine of occupied field is relevant for entries in the Concurrent List where both Parliament and State Legislatures have power.

questions.q: Which Article directs the State to promote the development of the Hindi language?
questions.e: Article 351 imposes a duty upon the Centre to promote the spread and development of the Hindi language.

questions.q: The 97th Amendment Act (2011) inserted which new Part in the Constitution?
questions.e: The 97th Amendment Act of 2011 added a new Part IX-B entitled "The Co-operative Societies".

questions.q: Which Ministry is the 'central personnel agency' in the Government of India?
questions.e: The Ministry of Personnel is the central personnel agency in the Government of India.

questions.q: Who is regarded as the 'Father of All-India Services'?
questions.e: Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel was the chief protagonist of All-India Services and is regarded as their 'Father'.

questions.q: Which Article empowers the Parliament to create new All-India Services?
questions.e: Article 312 of the Constitution authorizes the Parliament to create new All-India Services based on a resolution by the Rajya Sabha.

questions.q: According to the 'Doctrine of Pleasure' (Article 310), members of the civil services of the Centre hold office during the pleasure of:
questions.e: According to Article 310, members of the civil services of the Centre hold office during the pleasure of the President.

questions.q: Which Article provides safeguards to civil servants against arbitrary dismissal or removal?
questions.e: Article 311 provides two safeguards to civil servants against arbitrary dismissal from their posts.

questions.q: Under Article 311, a civil servant cannot be dismissed by an authority:
o: Superior to that by which they were appointed
Subordinate to that by which they were appointed
questions.e: A safeguard under Article 311 is that a civil servant cannot be dismissed by an authority subordinate to that by which he/she was appointed.

questions.q: In the 'Nagendra Rao case' (1994), the Supreme Court adopted a liberal approach regarding:
questions.e: In the Nagendra Rao case (1994), the Supreme Court adopted a liberal approach with respect to the tortious liability of the State.

questions.q: Which high-powered body is assigned the job of fixing boundaries of territorial constituencies?
questions.e: The job of delimitation (fixing boundaries) is assigned to a high-powered body known as the Delimitation Commission.

questions.q: The orders of the Delimitation Commission:
o: Can be modified by the Lok Sabha
Require approval from the Rajya Sabha
Can be challenged in High Courts
Cannot be challenged in any court
questions.e: The orders of the Delimitation Commission have the force of law and cannot be challenged in any court.

questions.q: How many members are in the Election Commission of India at present?
questions.e: The Election Commission of India is currently a three-member body, with one Chief Election Commissioner and two Election Commissioners.

questions.q: Who appoints the Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners?
questions.e: The President of India appoints the Chief Election Commissioner and the Election Commissioners.

questions.q: Which officer supervises the election work in a specific district?
questions.e: The District Election Officer (DEO) supervises the election work in a district.

questions.q: The 'Model Code of Conduct' for elections was agreed to by political parties in which year?
questions.e: The Model Code of Conduct was agreed to by all the political parties in 1968.

questions.q: Which system is used for elections to the Lok Sabha in India?
questions.e: Elections to the Lok Sabha are carried out using a first-past-the-post electoral system.

questions.q: Which Act was enacted to provide for the allocation of seats in the House of the People and State Assemblies?
questions.e: The Representation of the People Act, 1950 was enacted to provide for the allocation of seats in legislatures and the registration of electors.

questions.q: The 'Indrajit Gupta Committee' (1998) recommended:
questions.e: The Indrajit Gupta Committee (1998) upheld the argument for the introduction of state funding of elections.

questions.q: Which constitutional amendment reduced the voting age from 21 to 18 years?
questions.e: The 61st Constitutional Amendment Act of 1988 reduced the voting age from 21 to 18 years.

questions.q: 'None of the Above' (NOTA) option was introduced following directions from which body?
questions.e: According to the directions of the Supreme Court, the Election Commission made provision for the NOTA option in ballot papers/EVMs.

questions.q: Which year saw the introduction of the 'Electoral Bond Scheme' in the budget?
questions.e: The Electoral Bond Scheme was announced in the 2017 budget and notified in 2018.

questions.q: The 'Gujral Doctrine' (1996) is a roadmap for India's relations with:
questions.e: The Gujral Doctrine is a roadmap to guide India's foreign relations with its immediate smaller neighbours.

questions.q: Which Prime Minister chaired the National Integration Council in its first meeting in 1962?
questions.e: The NIC was constituted in 1961 and held its first meeting in 1962, chaired by the Prime Minister.

questions.q: The 91st Amendment Act (2003) limited the size of the Council of Ministers to what percentage of the total strength of the Lok Sabha?
questions.e: The 91st Amendment Act of 2003 provided that the total number of ministers shall not exceed 15 per cent of the total strength of the Lok Sabha.

questions.q: Under the 'Doctrine of Basic Structure', which of the following cannot be amended by Parliament?
o: The secular character of the Constitution
The age of retirement for judges
questions.e: In the S.R. Bommai case, the court held that secularism is part of the basic structure and hence cannot be destroyed by amendments.

questions.q: In which case did the Supreme Court rule that 'Right to Privacy' is a fundamental right?
questions.e: In the Justice K.S. Puttaswamy case (2017), the Supreme Court declared the right to privacy as a fundamental right under Article 21.

questions.q: Which judgment struck down the practice of 'Triple Talaq' as unconstitutional?
questions.e: In the Shayara Bano case (2017), the Supreme Court declared triple talaq (talaq-e-biddat) as unconstitutional.

questions.q: The 'Vishaka Guidelines' (1997) were related to:
o: Sexual harassment of women at workplace
questions.e: The Vishaka case (1997) resulted in guidelines to prevent sexual harassment of working women until suitable legislation was enacted.

questions.q: Which case declared that Article 21 is the 'sole repository' of the right to life during an emergency?
questions.e: In the A.D.M. Jabalpur case (1976), the court held that Article 21 is the sole repository of the right to life against the state.

questions.q: The 102nd Amendment Act (2018) conferred constitutional status on which commission?
questions.e: The 102nd Amendment Act of 2018 conferred constitutional status on the National Commission for Backward Classes by inserting Article 338-B.

questions.q: Which Article empowers the Governor to authorize the use of Hindi in High Court proceedings?
questions.e: Article 348 enables the governor of a state, with the previous consent of the President, to authorize the use of Hindi in High Court proceedings.

questions.q: The 'Doctrine of Harmonious Construction' is a rule of:
questions.e: The doctrine of harmonious construction is also called the rule of avoidance of conflict.

questions.q: Which body has the power to create a new All-India Service if a resolution is passed by the Rajya Sabha?
questions.e: Article 312 authorizes the Parliament to create new All-India Services based on a resolution by the Rajya Sabha.

questions.q: Under Article 311, the safeguard of inquiry is NOT available if a civil servant is dismissed due to:
questions.e: The safeguard of holding an inquiry is not available where a civil servant is dismissed on the ground of conduct which led to conviction on a criminal charge.

questions.q: Which doctrine is based on the English Common Law maxim "the King can do no wrong"?
questions.e: The traditional immunity of the Company (and later the State) was based on the maxim "the King can do no wrong".

questions.q: Which high-powered body's orders have the force of law and cannot be challenged in court?
questions.e: The orders of the Delimitation Commission have the force of law and cannot be challenged in any court.

questions.q: What is the standard duration for a newly established Law Commission?
questions.e: Law Commissions are established for a fixed tenure, typically three years.

questions.q: Which Article directs the State to provide instruction in the mother-tongue at the primary stage?
questions.e: Article 350A directs that states should provide adequate facilities for instruction in the mother-tongue at the primary stage for linguistic minorities.

questions.q: Who is considered the 'Father of All-India Services'?
questions.e: Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel was the chief protagonist of All-India Services and is regarded as their 'Father'.

questions.q: The 91st Amendment Act (2003) limited the size of a state's Council of Ministers to not less than:
questions.e: The 91st Amendment Act provides that the number of ministers in a state shall not be less than 12.

questions.q: Which Schedule of the Constitution contains the Anti-Defection Law?
questions.e: The Tenth Schedule, added by the 52nd Amendment Act, contains the provisions of the Anti-Defection Law.

questions.q: The 'Gujral Doctrine' (1996) is associated with which policy?
questions.e: The Gujral Doctrine is a milestone in India's foreign policy propounded in 1996.

questions.q: Which autonomous body was set up in 1992 to promote communal harmony?
questions.e: The National Foundation for Communal Harmony (NFCH) was set up in 1992 to promote national integration.

questions.q: The 105th Amendment Act (2021) modified provisions related to:
o: Socially and educationally backward classes (OBC lists)
questions.e: The 105th Amendment Act of 2021 modified provisions regarding the specification of socially and educationally backward classes.

questions.q: Which Article of the Constitution provides for a special officer for linguistic minorities to investigate matters relating to constitutional safeguards?
questions.e: According to the Constitution, the President should appoint a special officer for linguistic minorities. This officer investigates all matters relating to the constitutional safeguards for linguistic minorities and reports to the President.

questions.q: In which 2014 case did the Supreme Court declare transgenders as 'third gender' and upheld their right to decide their self-identified gender?
questions.e: In the National Legal Services Authority case (2014), the Supreme Court declared transgenders along with Hijaras/Eunuchs as 'third gender'. The court upheld their right to decide their self-identified gender and directed the government to grant legal recognition to their gender identity.

questions.q: The 99th Constitutional Amendment Act (2014) and the National Judicial Appointments Commission (NJAC) Act were declared unconstitutional in which case?
questions.e: In the Supreme Court Advocates-on-Record Association case (2015), also known as the Fourth Judges case, the court declared the 99th Amendment Act and the NJAC Act as unconstitutional and void. This judgment restored the earlier 'collegium system' of appointment of judges.

questions.q: Which landmark 1951 judgment led to the 1st Amendment Act and the insertion of Article 15(4) to allow for the advancement of backward classes?
questions.e: The Champakam Dorairajan case (1951) struck down communal reservations in educational institutions. This led to the 1st Amendment Act (1951), which inserted Clause (4) in Article 15 to permit the state to make special provisions for the advancement of socially and educationally backward classes.

questions.q: In the 1960 Berubari Union case, the Supreme Court ruled that Article 3 does NOT cover which of the following?
o: Diminishing the area of a state
Increasing the area of a state
Cession of Indian territory to a foreign country
questions.e: The Supreme Court ruled that the power of Parliament under Article 3 to diminish the area of a state does not cover cession of Indian territory to a foreign country. Territory can be ceded to a foreign state only by an amendment under Article 368.

questions.q: Which judgment overruled the restrictive interpretation of 'personal liberty' in A.K. Gopalan case and established the 'golden triangle' rule?
questions.e: The Maneka Gandhi case (1978) overruled the A.K. Gopalan case by taking a wider interpretation of Article 21. It firmly established the 'golden triangle' rule, which is the inter-relation of Articles 14, 19, and 21.

questions.q: The 'rarest of rare cases' doctrine for the death penalty was influenced by which case?
questions.e: In the Bachan Singh case (1980), the Supreme Court ruled that the death penalty in Section 302 of the IPC is not unreasonable but must be confined to the 'rarest of rare cases'.

questions.q: Which 1980 judgment invalidated Clauses (4) and (5) of Article 368, which sought to give Parliament unlimited power to amend the Constitution?
questions.e: In the Minerva Mills case (1980), the Supreme Court invalidated Clauses (4) and (5) of Article 368, holding that the limited power of Parliament to amend the Constitution is a basic feature.

questions.q: Which judgment led to the enactment of the Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Divorce) Act, 1986?
questions.e: The Shah Bano case (1985) ruled that a Muslim husband is liable to pay maintenance to his divorced wife. This led to the enactment of the Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Divorce) Act, 1986.

questions.q: The Supreme Court issued the 'Vishaka Guidelines' to address which issue due to a legislative vacuum?
o: Sexual harassment of women at workplace
questions.e: In the Vishaka case (1997), the Supreme Court held that sexual harassment of women at workplace is a violation of Articles 15 and 21. It provided detailed guidelines to be followed until suitable legislation was enacted.

questions.q: Which case directed the government to confer statutory status upon the Central Vigilance Commission (CVC)?
questions.e: In the Vineet Narain case (1997), also known as the Jain Hawala case, the Supreme Court directed that statutory status should be conferred upon the CVC.

questions.q: The Supreme Court judgment in the 'Association for Democratic Reforms case' (2002) led to which electoral requirement?
o: Mandatory disclosure of criminal antecedents and assets by candidates
questions.e: In the Association for Democratic Reforms case (2002), the Supreme Court held that voters have a right to know about the antecedents of candidates. It directed the Election Commission to make it mandatory for candidates to furnish information on criminal cases, assets, and educational qualifications.

questions.q: Which 2006 case led to the introduction of police reforms and the directive to set up a State Security Commission?
questions.e: In the Prakash Singh case (2006), the Supreme Court issued seven directives aimed at bringing in police reforms to ensure the police machinery functions without political interference.

questions.q: In which case did the Supreme Court declare 'talaq-e-biddat' (Triple Talaq) as unconstitutional?
questions.e: In the Shayara Bano case (2017), the Supreme Court declared triple talaq (talaq-e-biddat) as unconstitutional and violative of the fundamental right under Article 14.

questions.q: The judgment in 'K.S. Puttaswamy case' (2017) recognized which right as an integral part of the right to life?
questions.e: In the K.S. Puttaswamy case (2017), the Supreme Court declared the right to privacy as a fundamental right protected as an intrinsic part of the right to life and personal liberty under Article 21.

questions.q: Which 2018 judgment decriminalized consensual sexual acts of adults of the same sex by striking down Section 377 in part?
questions.e: In the Navtej Singh Johar case (2018), the Supreme Court decriminalized homosexuality and partly struck down Section 377 of the IPC in so far as it criminalized consensual sexual acts of adults of the same sex.

questions.q: The 2018 'Joseph Shine case' dealt with the decriminalization of which offence?
questions.e: In the Joseph Shine case (2018), the Supreme Court decriminalized adultery by striking down Section 497 of the IPC and Section 198(2) of the CrPC.

questions.q: In which case did the Supreme Court award the entire disputed land in Ayodhya for the construction of a temple?
questions.e: In the M. Siddiq case (2019), the Supreme Court awarded the entire 2.77 acres of disputed land in Ayodhya for the construction of a Ram Mandir.

questions.q: Which 2020 judgment addressed the suspension of internet services in Jammu and Kashmir?
o: Internet and Mobile Association of India case
questions.e: In the Anuradha Bhasin case (2020), the Supreme Court ruled on the suspension of internet services, stating that freedom of speech over the medium of internet enjoys constitutional protection under Article 19(1)(a).

questions.q: The 'Doctrine of Severability' is based on which Article of the Constitution?
questions.e: Article 13 is the basis of the doctrine of severability, which resolve the problem of the validity of laws declared unconstitutional.

questions.q: Which doctrine states that a pre-constitutional law inconsistent with a fundamental right is not dead but remains dormant?
questions.e: The doctrine of eclipse is based on the notion that a pre-constitutional law inconsistent with a fundamental right is overshadowed or eclipsed and remains dormant but not dead.

questions.q: The 'Doctrine of Pith and Substance' is primarily used to determine the competence of the legislature when laws:
o: Are not signed by the Governor
questions.e: The doctrine of pith and substance is applied when the validity of a law is challenged on the grounds of encroachment into another sphere, focusing on the true nature and character of the law as a whole.

questions.q: Which doctrine states that what cannot be done directly cannot be done indirectly?
questions.e: The whole doctrine of colourable legislation is based upon the maxim that "you cannot do indirectly, what you cannot do directly".

questions.q: The 'Doctrine of Territorial Nexus' is rated to which Article?
questions.e: The doctrine of territorial nexus is related to Article 245, which deals with the extent of laws made by the Parliament and the State Legislatures.

questions.q: According to the 'Doctrine of Implied Prohibition', applied in USA and Australia, residuary powers are left to:
questions.e: In USA and Australia, the doctrine of implied prohibition means only the powers of the Central Legislature are enumerated, and the residuary powers are left to the State Legislature.

questions.q: Which doctrine allows a court to overrule an old precedent from a future date only and not retrospectively?
questions.e: The doctrine of prospective overruling enables a court to overrule an old precedent from a future date only so that the validity of past transactions is not affected.

questions.q: The 'Doctrine of Harmonious Construction' is applied when:
o: There is a conflict between different provisions of the Constitution
A state law violates a central law
questions.e: When different provisions of the Constitution are found to be in conflict with each other, the courts interpret them harmoniously to avoid conflictual implications.

questions.q: Which doctrine suggests that the Constitution should be interpreted as a living and organic thing?
questions.e: The doctrine of liberal interpretation spirit should inspire the interpreters of the Constitution, assuming that the Constitution is a living and organic thing.

questions.q: The 'Doctrine of Creative Interpretation' was significantly manifested in which landmark case regarding basic structure?
questions.e: Another significant manifestation of the doctrine of creative interpretation is the judgement in the Kesavananda Bharati case (1973), which innovated the 'doctrine of basic structure'.

questions.q: Which Article provides that the law declared by the Supreme Court shall be binding on all courts in India?
questions.e: Article 141 of the Constitution incorporates the doctrine of precedent, stating that the law declared by the Supreme Court is binding on all courts.

questions.q: The 102nd Amendment Act (2018) conferred constitutional status on which body?
questions.e: The 102nd Amendment Act of 2018 conferred constitutional status on the National Commission for Backward Classes by inserting Article 338-B.

questions.q: Which Article of the Constitution deals with the reservation of seats for SCs and STs in the Lok Sabha?
questions.e: Article 330 deals with the reservation of seats for scheduled castes and scheduled tribes in the House of the People (Lok Sabha).

questions.q: Under the 91st Amendment Act (2003), the total number of ministers in a state shall NOT be less than:
questions.e: The 91st Amendment Act provides that the number of ministers, including the Chief Minister, in a state shall not be less than 12.

questions.q: Which committee was headed by M.N. Venkatachaliah to review the Constitution?
questions.e: The National Commission to Review the Working of the Constitution (NCRWC) was set up in 2000 and headed by M.N. Venkatachaliah.

questions.q: The NCRWC recommended that the retirement age of High Court judges should be increased to:
questions.e: The NCRWC recommended that the retirement age of the judges of high courts and Supreme Court should be increased to 65 and 68 respectively.

questions.q: Which type of pressure groups involve spontaneous breakthroughs like riots or assassinations?
questions.e: By anomic pressure groups, we mean more or less a spontaneous breakthrough into the political system such as riots or demonstrations.

questions.q: In the 1973 Kesavananda Bharati case, the Supreme Court declared which part of Section 3 of the 25th Amendment Act as invalid?
questions.e: In the Kesavananda Bharati case, the court held the first part of Section 3 of the 25th Amendment Act as valid but the second part as invalid.

questions.q: Which judgment struck down Clause (4) of Article 329A that removed election disputes involving the PM from judicial review?
questions.e: In the Indira Nehru Gandhi case (1975), the Supreme Court struck down clause (4) of Article 329A because it affected the basic structure of the constitution.

questions.q: The 'doctrine of rarest of rare cases' for death penalty was influence by which case?
questions.e: The Bachan Singh case (1980) led to the laying down of the doctrine of 'rarest of rare cases' for awarding the death penalty.

questions.q: Which judgment held that Article 21 is a protection only against the executive and NOT against the legislature?
questions.e: In the A.K. Gopalan case (1950), the court ruled that Article 21 is a protection only against the executive and not against the legislature.

questions.q: The 104th Amendment Act (2019) extended the reservation for SCs and STs in legislatures until the year:
questions.e: Under the 104th Amendment Act of 2019, the provision of reservation for SCs and STs is to last until the year 2030.

questions.q: Which Article provides that every bill introduced in Parliament must be accompanied by a Hindi translation?
questions.e: The Official Languages Act of 1963 lays down that every bill introduced in the Parliament is to be accompanied by a Hindi translation .

questions.q: The 'Look East Policy' was upgraded to 'Act East Policy' in which year?
questions.e: In 2014, the Modi Government upgraded India's "Look East Policy" and re-named it as the "Act East Policy".

questions.q: Which state has a special provision under Article 371-C?
questions.e: Article 371-C makes special provisions for the state of Manipur.

questions.q: The 'Gujral Doctrine' of 1996 focuses on India's relations with:
questions.e: The Gujral Doctrine advocates that India should extend unilateral concessions to its smaller neighbours on the basis of non-reciprocity .

questions.q: According to the 91st Amendment Act, a member disqualified on ground of defection is also disqualified from:
questions.e: The 91st Amendment Act (2003) provided that a member disqualified on the ground of defection shall also be disqualified to hold any remunerative political post.

questions.q: Which Article empowers the Parliament to establish a Central University in Andhra Pradesh?
questions.e: Article 371-E empowers the Parliament to provide for the establishment of a Central University in the state of Andhra Pradesh.

questions.q: The 'Doctrine of Implied Powers' is based on the maxim that whoever grants a thing is deemed also to grant:
o: That without which the grant itself would be of no effect
questions.e: The doctrine of implied powers is based on the maxim that "whoever grants a thing is deemed also to grant that without which the grant itself would be of no effect".

questions.q: Which judgment struck down Section 66A of the IT Act (2000) as violative of freedom of speech?
questions.e: In the Shreya Singhal case (2015), the Supreme Court struck down section 66A of the Information Technology Act (2000) as violative of the freedom of speech and expression.

questions.q: The 97th Amendment Act (2011) gave constitutional status to:
questions.e: The 97th Constitutional Amendment Act of 2011 gave a constitutional status and protection to co-operative societies.

questions.q: In which case did the Supreme Court strike down Section 66A of the IT Act, 2000 as violative of freedom of speech?
o: Justice K.S. Puttaswamy case Lily Thomas case Shayara Bano case
questions.e: In the Shreya Singhal case (2015), the Supreme Court struck down Section 66A of the Information Technology Act (2000) as it was violative of the freedom of speech and expression.

questions.q: Which case ruled that "Secularism" is part of the basic structure of the Constitution?
o: Kesavananda Bharati case Indira Nehru Gandhi case
S.R. Bommai case  Minerva Mills case
questions.e: In the S.R. Bommai case (1994), the Supreme Court laid down that secularism is a part of the basic structure of the constitution.

questions.q: The first backward classes commission was appointed in 1953 under the chairmanship of:
questions.e: The first backward classes commission was appointed in 1953 under the chairmanship of Kaka Kalelkar.

questions.q: The Law Commission of India is established by the order of:
o: The President of India The Parliament The Central Government
questions.e: The Law Commission of India is a non-statutory advisory body. It is established by the order of the Central Government from time to time for a fixed tenure.

questions.q: Under Article 372 of the Constitution, what happens to pre-Constitution laws?
o: They are replaced by British laws.
They shall remain in force until amended or repealed
questions.e: Article 372 of the Constitution provides that the pre-Constitution laws shall remain in force until they are amended or repealed.

questions.q: Who was the Chairman of the 22nd Law Commission of India?
o: Justice B.S. Chauhan Justice Ritu Raj Awasthi
questions.e: Justice Ritu Raj Awasthi served as the Chairman of the Twenty-Second Law Commission of India.

questions.q: The Chairman and full-time members of the Law Commission are generally:
o: Active politicians from the ruling party.
Serving or retired judges of the Supreme Court or High Courts
Foreign legal experts nominated by the UN.
Senior bureaucrats from the Indian Administrative Service.
questions.e: The Chairman and full-time members of the Commission are either serving or retired judges of the Supreme Court or High Courts, or legal experts, jurists, or professors of law.

questions.q: Which official belongs to the Indian Legal Service and holds the rank of Secretary or Additional Secretary in the Law Commission?
questions.e: The Member-Secretary of the Law Commission belongs to the Indian Legal Service and holds the rank of either Additional Secretary or Secretary to the Government of India.

questions.q: What is a primary function of the Law Commission regarding Central Acts?
o: To revise Central Acts to simplify them and remove anomalies
To enforce Central Acts in states.
To appoint judges to the Central Administrative Tribunal.
questions.e: One of the functions of the Law Commission is to revise the Central Acts of general importance so as to simplify them and remove anomalies, ambiguities, and inequities.

questions.q: To whom does the Law Commission forward its final reports?
o: The President of India The Chief Justice of India The Ministry of Law and Justice
questions.e: The final report of the Law Commission is forwarded to the Government (Ministry of Law and Justice).

questions.q: The word 'delimitation' literally means the process of:
o: Fixing limits or boundaries of territorial constituencies
Counting the total population of a country.
Appointing members to the Election Commission.
questions.e: The word 'delimitation' literally means the act or process of fixing limits or boundaries of territorial constituencies in a country or a Province having a legislative body.

questions.q: Which body is technically another name for the Delimitation Commission?
questions.e: A body assigned the job of delimitation is known as a Delimitation Commission or a Boundary Commission.

questions.q: The Delimitation Commission is a:
o: Non-statutory advisory body Private non-governmental body
questions.e: The Delimitation Commission of India is a statutory (and not a constitutional) body established by the Central Government under the provisions of a law enacted by Parliament.

questions.q: Orders of the Delimitation Commission come into force on a date specified by the:
o: Chief Election Commissioner Chief Justice of India
questions.e: The orders of the Delimitation Commission come into force on a date specified by the President of India.

questions.q: Which Constitutional Amendment Act of 2001 froze the total number of seats in the Lok Sabha until 2026?
o: 42nd Amendment Act 44th Amendment Act 84th Amendment Act
questions.e: The 84th Constitutional Amendment Act of 2001 and the 87th Constitutional Amendment Act of 2003 provided that the total number of seats in the Lok Sabha based on the 1971 census remain unaltered until the first census after 2026.

questions.q: Who was the Chairperson of the Fourth Delimitation Commission established in 2002?
o: Justice Ranjana Prakash Desai Justice Kuldip Singh
Justice K.K. Mathew Justice H.R. Khanna
questions.e: Justice Kuldip Singh, a retired judge of the Supreme Court, was appointed as the Chairperson of the Fourth Delimitation Commission.

questions.q: Associate members of the Delimitation Commission in respect of each state include:
o: The Governor and the Chief Minister.
Ten members of the Rajya Sabha.
Five members of the Lok Sabha and five members of the State Legislative Assembly
questions.e: The Commission had ten associate members in respect of each state: five members of the Lok Sabha and five members of the State Legislative Assembly.

questions.q: Which of the following rights do associate members of the Delimitation Commission NOT have?
o: Right to attend meetings Right to provide suggestions Right to vote or sign orders
Right to travel with the commission
questions.e: Associate members of the Delimitation Commission do not have the right to vote or to sign any order of the Commission.

questions.q: Who was appointed as the Chairperson of the 2020 Delimitation Commission for J&K?
o: Justice Kuldip Singh Justice Ranjana Prakash Desai
questions.e: Justice Ranjana Prakash Desai, a retired judge of the Supreme Court, was appointed as the Chairperson of the 2020 Commission.

questions.q: Before the J&K Reorganisation Act, 2019, the delimitation of the State Legislative Assembly seats in J&K was governed by:
o: The Constitution of India The Constitution of J&K and J&K Representation of People Act, 1957
The Delimitation Act, 2002 The Indian Independence Act, 1947
questions.e: Until the special status was withdrawn, the delimitation of State Legislative Assembly seats was governed by the Constitution of J&K and the J&K Representation of People Act, 1957.

questions.q: How many seats in the J&K Legislative Assembly are kept reserved (remain vacant) for Pakistan occupied J&K?
questions.e: The J&K Reorganisation Act, 2019 provided that for the area of the UT of J&K under occupation of Pakistan, 24 seats in the Assembly shall remain vacant.

questions.q: The J&K Reorganisation Act, 2019 allows the Lieutenant Governor to nominate how many women members to the Assembly?
questions.e: There is a provision for nomination of 2 women members to the Assembly by the Lieutenant Governor if women are not adequately represented.

questions.q: On the basis of which census did the 2020 Delimitation Commission work for the UT of J&K?
questions.e: The present Delimitation Commission was entrusted with the work of delimiting constituencies in the UT of J&K on the basis of the 2011 census.

questions.q: According to the 2022 Delimitation Order, how many total Assembly constituencies are there in the UT of J&K?
questions.e: Out of the total 90 Assembly constituencies in the J&K, 43 are for the Jammu region and 47 are for the Kashmir region.

questions.q: Which new Parliamentary constituency was carved out by combining areas from both Kashmir and Jammu regions?
questions.e: Anantnag-Rajouri Parliamentary Constituency has been carved out by combining the Anantnag area of the Kashmir region and the Rajouri & Poonch area of the Jammu region.

questions.q: How many Assembly constituencies are reserved for the Scheduled Tribes (STs) in the UT of J&K as per the 2022 order?
questions.e: The Commission provided for the reservation of 9 Assembly constituencies for the STs (6 in Jammu and 3 in Kashmir).

questions.q: The Delimitation Commission recommended the provision of at least how many members from the Kashmiri migrant community in the J&K Assembly?
questions.e: The Commission recommended the provision of at least two members (one of them must be a female) from the community of Kashmiri migrants in the J&K Assembly.

questions.q: Which Ministry is the nodal ministry for the Central Information Commission?
o: Ministry of Home Affairs Ministry of Finance Ministry of Personnel
questions.e: According to Table 71.2, the Central Information Commission falls under the Ministry of Personnel.

questions.q: The National Commission for Scheduled Tribes (STs) falls under the administrative control of which Ministry?
o: Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment Ministry of Tribal Affairs
Ministry of Personnel Ministry of Home Affairs
questions.e: The National Commission for STs falls under the Ministry of Tribal Affairs.

questions.q: Which Ministry is the nodal agency for the Attorney General of India and the Election Commission of India?
o: Ministry of Personnel Ministry of Home Affairs Ministry of Law and Justice
questions.e: Both the Attorney General of India and the Election Commission of India fall under the Ministry of Law and Justice.

questions.q: The North Eastern Council (NEC) operates under the administrative control of which Ministry?
o: Ministry of Finance Ministry of External Affairs E...
Ministry of Home Affairs Ministry of Development of North Eastern Region (DONER)
questions.e: The North Eastern Council operates under the administrative control of the Union Ministry of Development of the North Eastern Region (DONER).

questions.q: Where is the Secretariat (Headquarters) of the North Eastern Council located?
o: Guwahati, Assam Imphal, Manipur Shillong, Meghalaya
questions.e: The Secretariat (Headquarters) of the North Eastern Council is located in Shillong, Meghalaya.

questions.q: By virtue of the 2002 Amendment, the North Eastern Council has been made the:
o: Legislative Body for the region Judicial Tribunal for water disputes
Security Council for the region Regional Planning Body
questions.e: By virtue of the 2002 Amendment, the Council has been made the Regional Planning Body for the north eastern region.

questions.q: Who nominates the Chairman of the North Eastern Council?
o: The Prime Minister The Union Home Minister The President of India
questions.e: The President of India nominates the Chairman of the North Eastern Council.

questions.q: Which official has served as the ex-officio Chairman of the North Eastern Council since July 2018?
o: The Minister of DONER The Governor of Meghalaya Ex...
The Prime Minister The Union Home Minister
questions.e: Since July 2018, the Union Home Minister is the ex-officio Chairman of the Council.

questions.q: While formulating regional plans, the North Eastern Council gives priority to projects that benefit:
o: Only foreign trade Only urban areas
Only the state where the HQ is located Two or more states
questions.e: While formulating regional plans, the Council shall give priority to schemes and projects which will benefit two or more states.

questions.q: Which Part of the Constitution contains provisions regarding "The Co-operative Societies"?
o: Part IX Part IX-A Part IX-B
questions.e: The 97th Amendment Act added a new Part IX-B in the Constitution entitled "The Co-operative Societies" (Articles 243-ZH to 243-ZT).

questions.q: Under Article 19, the right to form co-operative societies is a:
o: Legal right Directive Principle Fundamental Right
questions.e: The 97th Amendment Act of 2011 made the right to form co-operative societies a fundamental right under Article 19.

questions.q: What is the maximum number of directors allowed for a co-operative society board?
questions.e: The maximum number of directors of a co-operative society shall not exceed twenty-one

questions.q: How many seats are reserved for women on the board of every co-operative society?
questions.e: The state legislature shall provide for the reservation of one seat for SCs/STs and two seats for women on the board of every co-operative society having members from such categories.

questions.q: The term of office of elected members of a co-operative society board is:
questions.e: The term of office of elected members of the board and its office bearers shall be five years from the date of election.

questions.q: A co-operative society board cannot be superseded for a period exceeding:
questions.e: No board shall be superseded or kept under suspension for a period exceeding six months.

questions.q: The accounts of every co-operative society must be audited within how many months of the close of the financial year?
questions.e: The accounts of every co-operative society shall be audited within six months of the close of the financial year.

questions.q: The Gujarat High Court in 2013 (Rajendra Shah case) declared that the 97th Amendment inserting Part IX-B was:
o: Constitutionally valid Ultra vires the Constitution for want of state ratification
Only applicable to Union Territories A violation of the Basic Structure
questions.e: In the Rajendra Shah case (2013), the Gujarat High Court declared the 97th Amendment inserting Part IX-B ultra vires for want of the requisite ratification by the states under Article 368.

questions.q: Which Part of the Constitution deals with the Official Language?
o: Part XV Part XVI Part XVII
questions.e: Part XVII of the Constitution deals with the official language in Articles 343 to 351.

questions.q: According to Article 343, what is the official language of the Union?
questions.e: Hindi written in Devanagari script is to be the official language of the Union.

questions.q: The numerals used for official purposes of the Union must be:
o: Devanagari numerals International form of Indian numerals
questions.e: The form of numerals to be used for the official purposes of the Union has to be the international form of Indian numerals and not the Devanagari form.

questions.q: Who was the Chairman of the Official Language Commission appointed in 1955?
questions.e: In 1955, the President appointed an Official Language Commission under the chairmanship of B.G. Kher.

questions.q: The Official Languages Act was enacted in which year?
questions.e: Subsequently, the Parliament enacted the Official Languages Act in 1963

questions.q: For how long does the Official Languages Act (1963) enable the use of English?
o: Up to 1975 Up to 1990 Indefinitely (without any time-limit)
questions.e: Notably, the Official Languages Act (1963) enables the use of English indefinitely (without any time-limit).

questions.q: Until Parliament provides otherwise, all proceedings in the Supreme Court must be in:
questions.e: Until Parliament provides otherwise, all proceedings in the Supreme Court and in every high court are to be in the English language only.

questions.q: Who can authorize the use of Hindi in the proceedings of a High Court with the consent of the President?
o: The Chief Minister The State Legislature
The Chief Justice of India The Governor of the state
questions.e: The governor of a state, with the previous consent of the President, can authorise the use of Hindi or any other official language of the state, in the proceedings in the high court.

questions.q: Every bill introduced in the Parliament must be accompanied by:
o: A summary in all 22 languages A Hindi translation
A legal certificate from the CJI An English translation only
questions.e: Every bill introduced in the Parliament is to be accompanied by a Hindi translation.

questions.q: How many languages were originally specified in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution?
questions.e: At present, the Eighth Schedule specifies 22 languages, but originally it specified 14 languages.

questions.q: Which language was added to the Eighth Schedule by the 21st Amendment Act of 1967?
questions.e: Sindhi was added to the Eighth Schedule by the 21st Amendment Act of 1967

questions.q: Which Amendment Act added Bodo, Dogri, Maithili, and Santhali to the Eighth Schedule?
o: 71st Amendment Act 86th Amendment Act 92nd Amendment Act
questions.e: Bodo, Dogri, Maithili, and Santhali were added by the 92nd Amendment Act of 2003.

questions.q: The Committee of Parliament on Official Language consists of how many members?
questions.e: This Committee comprises of 30 members of Parliament (20 from Lok Sabha and 10 from Rajya Sabha).

questions.q: As a convention, who is elected as the Chairman of the Committee of Parliament on Official Language?
o: The Prime Minister The Union Home Minister
The Speaker of Lok Sabha The Minister of Culture E...
questions.e: As a convention, the Union Home Minister has been elected as Chairman of the Committee from time to time.

questions.q: Public services in India are classified into how many categories?
questions.e: The public services in India are classified into three categories: all-India services, Central services, and state services.

questions.q: Which All-India service was established in 1966?
o: Indian Administrative Service Indian Police Service Indian Forest Service
questions.e: In 1966, the Indian Forest Service was established as the third all-India service.

questions.q: Who is regarded as the 'Father of All-India Services'?
questions.e: Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel was the chief protagonist of All-India Services and came to be regarded as the 'Father of All-India Services'.

questions.q: Members of All-India Services are recruited and trained by:
o: The State Governments The Central Government
The UPSC only The Planning Commission
questions.e: The members of these Services are recruited and trained by the Central Government but are assigned to different states for work.

questions.q: Disciplinary action (imposition of penalties) against All-India Service officers can only be taken by:
o: The Governor The Chief Minister The Central Government
questions.e: The disciplinary action (imposition of penalties) against these officers can only be taken by the Central government.

questions.q: Which Central Service is considered the top most in terms of prestige and pay scale?
o: Indian Postal Service Indian Revenue Service Indian Foreign Service (IFS)
questions.e: It must also be mentioned here that the Indian Foreign Service (IFS) is the top most Central Service in terms of prestige, status, pay and emoluments.

questions.q: According to the 'Doctrine of Pleasure' (Article 310), members of All-India services hold office during the pleasure of:
questions.e: According to Article 310, members of the defence services, the civil services of the Centre and the all-India services... hold office during the pleasure of the President.

questions.q: Which Article provides safeguards to civil servants against dismissal or removal by an authority subordinate to that which appointed them?
questions.e: Article 311 provides two safeguards: (a) a civil servant cannot be dismissed or removed by an authority subordinate to that by which he/she was appointed.

questions.q: Which constitutional amendment act abolished the provision for a second opportunity to make representation against the punishment proposed for a civil servant?
o: 44th Amendment Act 52nd Amendment Act 73rd Amendment Act
questions.e: The 42nd Amendment Act of 1976 abolished the provision for second opportunity (the right to make representation against the punishment proposed).

questions.q: Succession to all property and assets that were vested in the Dominion of India now vest in:
questions.e: All property and assets that were vested in the Dominion of India... became vested in the Union.

questions.q: What happens to property found without any owner (Bona Vacantia)?
o: It vests in the state if situated there, or in the Union
It is given to the finder.
It is returned to the British Crown.
It is auctioned by the Supreme Court.
questions.e: Property found without any owner (bona vacantia) would now vest in the state if the property is situated there, and in the Union, in any other case.

questions.q: All lands and minerals under the territorial waters of India vest in:
questions.e: All lands, minerals and other things of value under the waters of the ocean within the territorial waters... vests in the Union.

questions.q: India's territorial waters extend to a distance of how many nautical miles?
questions.e: India's territorial waters extend to a distance of 12 nautical miles from the appropriate baseline.

questions.q: Which amendment abolished the constitutional obligation to pay compensation for compulsory acquisition of private property (except in specific cases)?
questions.e: The 44th Amendment Act (1978) abolished the constitutional obligation to pay compensation except in cases of minority educational institutions or land within ceiling limits.

questions.q: Which Article provides that the Government of India may sue or be sued by the name of the 'Union of India'?
questions.e: Article 300 of the Constitution deals with the suits by or against the Government in India. It lays down that the Government of India may sue or be sued by the name of the Union of India.

questions.q: Contracts made in the exercise of executive power of the Union must be executed on behalf of:
questions.e: Contracts must be expressed to be made by the president or governor and executed on behalf of the president or governor.

questions.q: The government in India can be sued for torts committed by officials only in the exercise of:
o: Any function without exception Judicial functions only
questions.e: Therefore, the government... in India can be sued for torts (civil wrongs) committed by its officials only in the exercise of its non-sovereign functions.

questions.q: Which landmark 1994 case criticized the doctrine of sovereign immunity and held the State liable for damage due to negligent acts of servants?
o: Shah Bano case Kesavananda Bharati case
questions.e: In Nagendra Rao case (1994), the Supreme Court criticised the doctrine of sovereign immunity and adopt a liberal approach with respect to the tortuous liability of the State.

questions.q: What advance notice is required to start civil proceedings against the President or a Governor for personal acts?
questions.e: Civil proceedings can be started against them during their term of office in respect of their personal acts after giving two months' advance notice.

questions.q: Judicial officers enjoy immunity from liability for official acts under which Act?
o: The Constitution of India The Judicial Officers Protection Act (1850)
The Indian Penal Code The Contempt of Courts Act E...
questions.e: The Judicial Officers Protection Act (1850) lays down that no judge... shall be liable to be sued in any civil court for any act done by him in the discharge of his official duty.

questions.q: Which Part of the Constitution contains special provisions for SCs, STs, BCs and Anglo-Indians?
o: Part III Part IV Part XVI
questions.e: These special provisions are contained in Part XVI of the Constitution from Articles 330 to 342A.

questions.q: Who has the power to specify what castes or tribes are to be treated as SCs or STs in each state?
o: The Parliament The Governor The President
questions.e: It leaves to the President the power to specify as to what castes or tribes in each state and union territory are to be treated as the SCs and STs.

questions.q: Any inclusion or exclusion of any caste from the Presidential notification for SCs/STs can be done only by:
o: A subsequent Presidential notification The State Legislature The Parliament
questions.e: But, any inclusion or exclusion of any caste or tribe from Presidential notification can be done only by the Parliament and not by a subsequent Presidential notification.

questions.q: Reservation for SCs and STs in legislatures was originally to operate for how many years?
questions.e: Originally, this provision of reservation was to operate for ten years (i.e., up to 1960) only.

questions.q: The combined National Commission for SCs and STs was bifurcated by which amendment?
o: 42nd Amendment Act 61st Amendment Act 89th Amendment Act
questions.e: Previously, the Constitution provided for a combined National Commission for SCs and STs. The 89th Amendment Act of 2003 bifurcated the combined commission into two separate bodies.

questions.q: Which Article provides for the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes?
questions.e: The President should also set up a National Commission for the STs to investigate all matters relating to the Constitutional safeguards for the STs and to report to him/her (Article 338-A).

questions.q: Which Amendment Act conferred constitutional status on the National Commission for Backward Classes?
o: 91st Amendment Act 97th Amendment Act 102nd Amendment Act
questions.e: Later, the 102nd Amendment Act of 2018 conferred a constitutional status on the commission.

questions.q: Who was the Chairman of the Second Backward Classes Commission appointed in 1979?
questions.e: The second Backward Classes Commission was appointed in 1979 with B.P. Mandal as chairman.

questions.q: Article 371 provides special responsibility for the Governors of which two states?
o: Sikkim and Mizoram Andhra Pradesh and Telangana Ex...
Nagaland and Assam Maharashtra and Gujarat
questions.e: Under Article 371, the President is authorised to provide that the Governor of Maharashtra and that of Gujarat would have special responsibility.

questions.q: Article 371-A makes special provisions for which state?
questions.e: Article 371-A makes the following special provisions for Nagaland

questions.q: The special provisions for the state of Sikkim are mentioned under which Article?
questions.e: The 36th Constitutional Amendment Act of 1975 made Sikkim a full-fledged state... It included a new Article 371-F containing special provisions.

questions.q: The minimum number of seats in the Sikkim Legislative Assembly is fixed at:
questions.e: The Sikkim Legislative Assembly is to consist of not less than 30 members

questions.q: Article 371-G specifies special provisions for:
questions.e: Article 371-G specifies the following special provisions for Mizoram
